en: The Sūtra on the Fundamental Characteristics of Dependent Origination, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada. The Buddha...
He then addressed the bhikṣus:

"Originally there was craving, which I did not see and did not understand; now I see that existence proceeds from craving. Even if this original craving were non-existent today, it would still result in existence; now I see this clearly."
From this primary cause and condition, craving for existence is brought about. Craving for existence, monks!
arises from the primary cause of existence; it does not arise without a primary cause. And what, monks, is that?
From what does craving for existence arise?
It is said to be from delusion. "Delusion also, bhikkhus!"
There is that which has a basis from which it arises; it is not without a basis.
What, bhikṣu, is the basis from which delusion arises?
This refers to the five hindrances.
"Monks, these five hindrances also have a root from which they arise; they do not exist without a root."
"What, monks, are the five hindrances that lead to existence?
They are the three types of unwholesome conduct."
“Monks, the three types of unwholesome conduct also have a basis from which they arise; they do not exist without a basis.
What, monks, is that basis?”
From what do the three types of unwholesome conduct originate?
They arise from the non-restraint of the sense faculties.
"Bhikkhus, it is through the non-restraint of the sense faculties [that they arise]."
Furthermore, there are causes from which [this state] arises; it is not without a cause.
What, monks, is the lack of restraint of the sense faculties as a cause?
This means it is because of a lack of original mindfulness.
"Monks, even that which is not original mindfulness has an origin from which it comes; it is not without an origin."
What, monks, is that which leads away from right mindfulness?
It is lack of faith.
“Lack of faith, bhikkhus, also has its origin; it is not without an origin.
What, bhikkhus, is that origin?”
From what does lack of faith fundamentally arise?
It is said to be due to hearing about evil and what is not the Dharma.
"O Bhikṣus, it is from hearing what is not the Dharma!"
Furthermore, there are origins from which [unwholesome states] arise;
it is not that they have no origin. What, monks, are the origins from which unrighteousness arises through hearing?
This refers to the conduct of those who are not noble persons.
Even for those who are not noble persons, there is a basis from which it arises; it does not come about without a basis.
What is that basis, bhikṣus?
"Is it not from the company of the unvirtuous?
It is said that the unvirtuous person delights in socializing with the unvirtuous.
Thus, bhikkhus, when the assembly of the unvirtuous is full, the affairs of the unvirtuous become full."
When unwholesome deeds have reached fulfillment, they cause unrighteousness to reach fulfillment;
when unrighteousness has reached fulfillment, they cause lack of faith to reach fulfillment;
when lack of faith has reached fulfillment, they cause the failure to maintain original mindfulness to reach fulfillment.
When the fulfillment of not being mindful of one's original intention has occurred, it causes the fulfillment of not restraining the sense faculties;
when the fulfillment of not restraining the sense faculties has occurred, it causes the fulfillment of committing the three types of unwholesome conduct;
when the fulfillment of committing the three types of unwholesome conduct has occurred, it causes the fulfillment of the five hindrances.
When the five hindrances are fulfilled, delusion is made full;
when delusion is full, worldly craving is made full.
Thus, as this craving and delight become full, there is a gradual, progressive increase in the accumulation of existence.
“The wisdom and liberation that transcend the world also have a basis; it is not without a basis.
What is the basis for the wisdom and liberation that transcend the world?
It is said that the seven factors of enlightenment are the basis.”
"The seven factors of enlightenment have a basis; they do not lack a basis.
What is the basis for the seven factors of enlightenment?
It is the four foundations of mindfulness."
“The four foundations of mindfulness have a basis; they do not lack a basis.
What, monk, is the basis from which the four foundations of mindfulness arise?”
This refers to the three kinds of pure conduct.
"Bhikkhus, these three kinds of purity also have an origin from practice; they do not exist without an origin."
What, monks, are the three purities that have their basis?
They are said to be the guarding and restraint of the sense faculties.
“The guarding and restraint of the sense faculties also has a basis; it is not without a basis.
What, bhikṣus, is the basis for the guarding and restraint of the sense faculties?
This is said for the sake of fundamental mindfulness.
"Bhikkhus, fundamental mindfulness also has a basis; it is not without a basis."
What, monks, is the foundation of original mindfulness?
It is said to be the foundation of faith.
“Faith, bhikkhus, also has a basis; it is not without a basis.
What, bhikkhus, is that basis?”
Does faith have an original source?
It refers to the *Dharmasravana-sūtra* as its source.
The *Dharmasravana-sūtra* also has a source; it is not without a source.
What is the original text of the Sūtra on Hearing the Dharma?
It is the original text of serving the worthy.
Serving the worthy also has an original text; it is not without an original text.
What is the basis for associating with the noble?
It is the basis of associating with the noble assembly. "Thus it is, bhikṣus!"
By associating with the worthy, one is able to serve the worthy;
having served the worthy, one hears the words of the Dharma;
having heard the words of the Dharma, one attains the root of faith.
Having attained mastery over the bases, one then attains mindfulness of the bases;
having attained mindfulness of the bases, one then guards the sense faculties;
having guarded the sense faculties, one then attains the three purities.
Having attained the three purities, one then attains the four foundations of mindfulness;
having attained the foundation of the four foundations of mindfulness, one then possesses the seven factors of enlightenment;
having possessed the seven factors of enlightenment, one then attains unconditioned liberation and transcends the world.
"Thus is liberation that transcends the world; by turning back to the root again and again, one enables the transcendence of the world.
When the Buddha had spoken thus, the disciples received and practiced it.
This is the *Sūtra on the Fundamental Characteristics of Reliance*, as taught by the Buddha.
